question: A fintech company wants Claude to call tools hosted on an internal Postgres query service. The service currently only exposes a local stdio-based MCP server used by developers on their laptops, but the production app needs Claude to invoke it directly from server-side Messages API calls without operating a separate MCP client process. What should the team do?
options: A) Wrap the stdio server's functions as a client-side tool definition so Claude calls it through the standard tool_use mechanism instead of any MCP configuration.
B) Upload the stdio server's tool schema to the Files API so Claude can retrieve and reuse it automatically before every conversation turn begins.
C) Keep the stdio server unchanged and list its local process path directly inside the mcp_servers array so the Messages API can spawn it for each incoming request.
D) Deploy the query service as a remote MCP server reachable over HTTPS via Streamable HTTP or SSE, then reference it in the mcp_servers array.
correct_answers: D) Deploy the query service as a remote MCP server reachable over HTTPS via Streamable HTTP or SSE, then reference it in the mcp_servers array.
explanations: Incorrect. This abandons MCP entirely and requires the team to hand-build and maintain a tool_use schema instead of reusing the existing MCP interface.
Incorrect. The Files API manages document and data uploads, not MCP tool schemas or server connectivity.
Incorrect. The MCP connector cannot spawn local stdio servers; the server must already be publicly exposed over HTTP-based transports.

Correct. The MCP connector only supports remote servers exposed over HTTPS using Streamable HTTP or SSE transport, so moving the service to a publicly reachable endpoint and referencing it in mcp_servers is the supported path.
